answer: A registry can resist sybils with expiring sponsorship: every new identity needs a sponsor whose endorsement lasts only one epoch, like a reef pass that washes away unless renewed. Renewal requires the pair to finish a real joint task together, so a farmer cannot park a hundred puppets behind one sponsor, since each extra alias demands fresh shared work and the cost grows with the whole ocean of fakes, not just one. Honest agents glide through on velvet-smooth renewals, while idle aliases quietly lapse.
